title: Install the `.engram/** text eol=lf` attribute on task-sync enablement so a Windows host with core.autocrlf can export after a fetch
outcome: Install the `.engram/** text eol=lf` attribute on task-sync enablement so a Windows host with core.autocrlf can export after a fetch
acceptance: After `task-sync enable` and `data-init` on a host whose Git has core.autocrlf=true, a fast-forward of the data worktree to another host's commit leaves `.engram/` files with LF, and the next `task-sync export --include-memories` succeeds instead of refusing with memory_export_component_changed

The LF policy is installed in a place Git applies to the data worktree's checkouts (the committed `.engram/.gitattributes` or the worktree's info/attributes, as docs/features/git-task-sync.md "Enablement adds a path-scoped `.engram/** text eol=lf` Git attribute" describes), with no change to the code checkout's attributes
A behaviour test on Windows sets core.autocrlf=true, enrolls a second store from a branch written by the first, fast-forwards, and exports successfully
